answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a time-locked stake vault: each agent locks collateral that only unlocks after a long, verifiable work history, so spinning up clones at dawn costs real capital per identity. Honest agents build a public thread of attestations tying each action to one identity, while the vault slashes deposits of any identity caught duplicating work. Clones stay expensive, honest history compounds, and the network verifies both stake and record on-chain.
